findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at class definition, not per instance
findings.body: The field declaration `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` causes `timezone.now()` to be evaluated exactly once when the class body is executed (at module import time), not each time an `AssignmentSource` is constructed. Every instance created in the same process — including those produced by `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` during inbound webhooks — will share the same `queued` timestamp (the time the module was first imported). For a long-running web server this means `queued` is effectively a process start time, not the time the assignment was queued. The field is part of the serialized payload (`to_dict`/`from_dict`) and is clearly meant to record when the change was queued, so any future logic that relies on it (staleness checks, ordering, debugging) will be wrong. The fix is to use `field(default_factory=lambda: timezone.now())` from `dataclasses`.

findings.title: test_to_dict does not verify queued is per-instance and would not catch the mutable-default bug
findings.body: The test only asserts `result.get("queued") is not None`, which is trivially true even when every instance shares the same timestamp (the `queued` field is never None because it was populated at class definition). A stronger assertion — e.g. creating two `AssignmentSource` instances with a small `time.sleep` between them and verifying their `queued` values differ — would catch the dataclass default-evaluation bug. As written, the test gives a false sense of coverage for the `queued` field's semantics.

findings.title: Typo in test method name: 'inalid' should be 'invalid'
findings.body: The test method is named `test_from_dict_inalid_data`. The word 'inalid' is a typo for 'invalid'. This makes the test harder to find by name and looks unprofessional in test reports.

findings.title: No test for deassign cycle prevention (matching source integration)
findings.body: The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only exercises the assign path when the source integration matches the target. The deassign path in `GroupAssigneeManager.deassign` also threads `assignment_source` through to `sync_group_assignee_outbound`, and the `should_sync` cycle check applies to both assign and deassign, but there is no `test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign_with_matching_source_integration` (or equivalent) verifying that `sync_assignee_outbound` is NOT called when `deassign` is invoked with a matching source. Without this, a regression in the deassign wiring (e.g. dropping the `assignment_source` kwarg) would not be caught.
